nodes.label: Appraisal Tool Selection by Design
nodes.rationale: Exactly one tool per study, driven by the extracted design. tool:none is a legitimate common outcome, not a failure — applying AMSTAR-2 to a narrative review manufactures a critically_low that reads as a quality verdict on work that never claimed to be systematic.

nodes.label: RoB 2 (randomized trials)
nodes.rationale: Assessed per result and per outcome, for a stated effect of interest (assignment vs adherence); domain 2 branches on that choice. Signalling questions are answered first and the domain judgement derived from them, never reverse-engineered.

nodes.label: ROBINS-I (non-randomized studies)
nodes.rationale: Overall is the worst domain judgement — no averaging, no compensation. Judged against a hypothetical target trial written down before domain 1, which forces explicit confounder lists and time-zero alignment checks.

nodes.label: Target-Trial Framing
nodes.rationale: Writing down eligibility, treatment, assignment, outcome and follow-up before appraising turns vague judgement into deviation-from-a-specified-trial, surfacing immortal time and prevalent-user bias that would otherwise be assumed absent.

nodes.label: Newcastle-Ottawa Scale
nodes.rationale: The NOS defines no good/fair/poor thresholds; any cutoff is the reviewer's and must be declared before use. A star count is not a risk-of-bias judgement and must not be translated into 'low risk' in prose.

nodes.label: AMSTAR-2 (systematic reviews)
nodes.rationale: Rates confidence in the review's results, not certainty of the underlying evidence; a critically_low must not be restated as 'very low certainty' — that is GRADE's job.

nodes.label: Saying Unclear Honestly (rules U1-U4)
nodes.rationale: The single largest failure mode of automated appraisal is converting silence into reassurance. Absence of reporting is never evidence of low risk; three different silences (not reported, not assessable from this source, reported as absent) must be distinguished; never infer from journal, funder, sample size or registration.

nodes.label: Abstract-Only Restricted Appraisal
nodes.rationale: A record with five unclear domains and one weakly-supported judgement communicates less than an honest 'not appraised: abstract only', so tool:none is preferred when no domain is assessable. A truncation-detected HTML fetch is abstract-only, never 'partial full text'.

nodes.label: GRADE Certainty Rating
nodes.rationale: Rated per outcome across the body of studies, not per study. Five downgrade and three upgrade domains; no double-counting a problem under two domains; certainty is about the estimate, not importance — 'low certainty' never means 'no effect'.

nodes.label: GRADE Certainty Wording (verbatim shapes)
nodes.rationale: Fixed verb forms ('reduces' / 'probably reduces' / 'may reduce' / 'the evidence is very uncertain about') make certainty legible in prose and are the permitted evidence-side vocabulary at the hard wall.
